The *Seyyajātaka* (Ja 310) is a narrative belonging to the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional nidāna recorded in its opening blurb, the Buddha recounted this past-life story while residing at the Jetavana monastery outside Sāvatthī [SuttaCentral]. The tale was occasioned by a backsliding bhikkhu who, while walking on his alms round in the city, caught sight of a beautiful woman and subsequently grew discontented, abandoning his joy in the Dhamma [SuttaCentral]. The text is also explicitly referenced in the post-canonical *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.5.5, *Buddhaaviheṭhakapañha*) [SuttaCentral].

In terms of textual parallels and reuse, SuttaCentral notes passage-level correspondences with several other canonical texts: the *Lomasakassapajātaka* (Ja 433), the *Chavakajātaka* (Ja 309), the *Lābhagarahajātaka* (Ja 287), and the monastic training rule at *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya* 69 (Bu-Vb Sk69) [SuttaCentral]. The machine-computed analysis from DharmaNexus confirms this connection with Ja 433, identifying an identical 324-character passage alignment (§0.4–4.4 of Ja 310 with §2.1–5.4 of Ja 433, similarity 1.0) [DharmaNexus]. On SuttaCentral, four modern translations are cataloged across four languages [SuttaCentral]. The secondary literature passages in the present dossier do not provide direct analysis of Ja 310, referring instead to the homonymous *Seyyajātaka* (Ja 282) or addressing unrelated grammatical and Vinaya occurrences of the Pali term *seyyā*.
